title: Modular parallel README authoring skill from reademe-temp
hypotheses: README components can be drafted independently from shared repository evidence and assembled without competing writes.
Evidence reports and deterministic assembly can improve integration while the parent retains semantic responsibility.
A modular skill and template bundle may produce useful README outcomes even though its structure differs from the current canonical readme-review capability.
limitations: The imported skill is a candidate, not a released or automatically invocable README Labs capability.
Its initial forward test covered one local repository and a minimal three-component profile.
The catalog and validation rules may encode current section assumptions and must remain open to competing candidates.
